analysis:
Examined the SandboxSetupCommand.swift and SandboxSetupProgress.swift diffs and the full base/head text of the first file. The main security change is in SandboxSetupFlow.run for the `.fresh` case. The installer is downloaded and staged first via `withInstaller`, which uses `SandboxInstaller.stage` and removes the directory afterwards. It is then executed with `--plan` (requestAddonPlan, head lines 220-235) so the add-on can report sizing, and only after that does the confirmation prompt appear. This moves execution of a remotely fetched script as the Mac owner ahead of consent, which T-061/TB-013/A-019 cover, so I raised a finding. The CLI's own claim that it 'asks before installing anything' is technically true but hides the earlier code execution.

The plan output is parsed by `SandboxSizingPlan(line:)`. It is strictly typed with schema and event checks, but the `message` and `limit` strings come from an untrusted installer. They are printed to the terminal without control-character stripping, which is a minor escape-sequence injection concern at the same trust level as the installer. The plan values also drive the owner's decision, though the installer is already trusted for execution.

The `background` flag in SandboxSetupProgress.swift only changes advisory UI text about waiting for approval. It does not affect credentials, tokens or authorization. The `setvbuf` change is benign.

Not visible and needing review: `SandboxInstaller.planArguments`, `supportsPlan`, `stage` permissions, `SandboxChildProcess.run`, the environment passed to the child, and whether `--plan` is enforced by the installer or only by convention. Also unverified: `eligibility.refusal`, `estimatedPlan`, and whether `--yes` / `--linux-slots` options are forwarded to the plan run.

findings.detail: In the fresh-setup path, `withInstaller` downloads install.sh from the sandbox service. `sizeAndConfirm` then calls `requestAddonPlan`, which runs it with `/bin/sh <installer> --plan ...` as the Mac owner before the consent prompt (SandboxSetupCommand.swift:150-151, 220-226). Previously only static eligibility checks ran before the prompt, and the remote script ran only after the owner agreed. A misissued TLS certificate or a compromised sandbox service (T-061) can now run arbitrary code as the owner (A-019) on every `darkbloom sandbox setup`. That includes owners who would answer 'no', and the code runs before any trade-off text is shown. The `--plan` mode only limits what a well-behaved installer does; the code does not enforce it. Fix: do not run the remote script before consent. Either confirm first using the local estimate, or authenticate the installer (pinned signature or hash) before any execution. If the pre-consent run stays, update TB-013/T-061 to say that execution now precedes consent.
findings.title: Downloaded installer is now executed before the owner's confirmation
